question: What is a well-known health problem caused by an iron deficiency?

options.A: Rickets
options.B: Anemia
options.C: Goiter
options.D: Scurvy

explanation: Iron is needed to build hemoglobin in our red blood cells. Without enough iron, the blood can't carry oxygen well, leading to anemia and tiredness. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T006#GNS227_U1_T006_h7)

question: Why must a nurse use a filter needle when drawing medication from a glass ampoule?

options.A: To make the plunger move more smoothly inside the barrel
options.B: To filter out bacteria present in the room air
options.C: To change the chemical pH of the liquid medicine
options.D: To prevent tiny glass shards from entering the syringe

explanation: Snapping the neck of a glass ampoule creates microscopic shards. A filter needle traps these fragments so they are not injected into the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h4)

question: What is the main goal of community mobilisation in primary health care?

options.A: Empowering locals to take charge of health
options.B: Replacing traditional healers with doctors
options.C: Relying entirely on government funding
options.D: Imposing foreign medical standards

explanation: Community mobilisation focuses on enabling local populations to identify and solve their own health problems. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h1)

question: How should a nurse respond when a caregiver expresses fear and doubt about a routine vaccine?

options.A: Ignore the question and administer the injection without speaking
options.B: Listen with empathy, validate concerns, and provide clear factual information
options.C: Scold the caregiver for putting their child's life at immediate risk
options.D: Tell the caregiver that rumors are illegal and punishable by law

explanation: You've got this! Building trust through patience and gentle, honest education is always the best way to help caregivers feel confident. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T12#GNS313_U2_T12_h8)

question: Why is careful monitoring of IV fluids especially vital during labor for a mother with kidney disease?

options.A: Excess fluids stop the uterus from contracting normally after the baby is born
options.B: Compromised kidneys cannot handle fluid overload, increasing the risk of pulmonary edema
options.C: Too much intravenous fluid causes the infant's kidneys to stop working permanently
options.D: Intravenous fluids react badly with standard pain medications used in labor

explanation: Weakened kidneys can't get rid of extra water well, so giving too much IV fluid can cause it to back right up into her lungs. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T007#GNS226_U4_T007_h8)

question: How does melanin protect our skin cells from ultraviolet (UV) rays?

options.A: It absorbs and scatters UV rays before they damage cell DNA.
options.B: It freezes the skin surface to block hot sunlight.
options.C: It neutralizes sweat acids to stop sunburns.
options.D: It thickens the outer skin into a hard shell.

explanation: Well done! Melanin acts as your body's built-in umbrella, soaking up and scattering harmful UV rays away from your cell nuclei. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which common side effect of opioids do patients almost NEVER develop a tolerance to?

options.A: Nausea
options.B: Constipation
options.C: Euphoria
options.D: Sedation

explanation: While patients get used to the sleepiness and dizziness from opioids, the bowels stay slow. Always plan for laxatives! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T1#GNS223_U5_T1_h6)

question: What is the biggest risk of trying to estimate your injection usage from memory?

options.A: It automatically invalidates the nurse's practicing license
options.B: It causes immediate physical damage to safety boxes
options.C: It doubles the financial cost of purchasing new syringes
options.D: It distorts supply chain forecasts and leads to future stockouts

explanation: Spot on! If our recorded guesses are wrong, the central store will send the wrong quantity, leading to frustrating shortages. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h4)

question: Why is a longitudinal design great for studying chronic illnesses like heart disease?

options.A: It costs almost no money compared to other study methods
options.B: It guarantees that every single patient will be completely cured
options.C: It allows researchers to watch how the disease develops and progresses slowly over time
options.D: It requires only one afternoon of data collection at a clinic

explanation: Well done! Since chronic illnesses unfold gradually, tracking patients over a long period helps us understand the disease process clearly. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T11#GNS224_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is the main job of the alveoli in the breast?

options.A: Storing fat to give the breast shape
options.B: Synthesizing and secreting milk
options.C: Producing oxytocin for uterine contractions
options.D: Transporting milk directly to the skin surface

explanation: Spot on! The alveoli are tiny sac-like structures lined with special cells that actually make and secrete milk. You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T18#GNS121_U5_T18_h1)

question: Why does sitting a breathless patient up in a semi-Fowler's or high-Fowler's position help them?

options.A: It stops blood from flowing too quickly to the brain
options.B: It prevents dust particles from settling inside the windpipe
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any supplemental oxygen
options.D: It expands the chest cavity and eases the work of breathing

explanation: Brilliant! Sitting upright uses gravity to pull the diaphragm down, giving the lungs more room to fill up with air. [learn more](GST114_U6_T7#GST114_U6_T7_h7)

question: How did 20th-century pharmacology fundamentally differ from ancient healing practices?

options.A: It shifted from using crude natural mixtures to laboratory synthesis and targeted chemicals.
options.B: It abandoned all plant-based treatments in favor of spiritual healing.
options.C: It stopped testing medications on living tissues before human use.
options.D: It relied exclusively on oral traditions rather than written science.

explanation: Twentieth-century science moved past trial-and-error plant use to design and synthesize targeted chemical compounds in laboratories. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is compulsory before a patient takes part in a nursing research study?

options.A: A financial deposit
options.B: Informed consent
options.C: Hospital employment
options.D: A government passport

explanation: Patients must always be fully informed about the study and willingly agree to participate of their own free will. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h7)

question: Which part of the brain acts as the emotional alarm system that triggers the fight-or-flight response during anxiety?

options.A: The pituitary gland
options.B: The cerebellum
options.C: The medulla oblongata
options.D: The amygdala

explanation: Spot on! The amygdala is our emotional radar. It processes threats and sounds the alarm early when we feel anxious. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T1#GNS324_U4_T1_h1)

question: A community nurse notices a family pulled their 12-year-old daughter out of school while keeping her younger brother in class. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: Cultural preference for investing in male education and financial dependence of women
options.B: An official policy granting free education exclusively to male children
options.C: Government regulations prohibiting females from attending secondary school
options.D: Medical evidence showing girls learn better through home apprenticeships

explanation: When money is tight, families with gender bias often sacrifice a daughter's schooling to pay for the son's. As nurses, spotting these patterns helps us guide the family better. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T5#GNS225_U5_T5_h4)

question: What is a vital nursing duty once a patient is physically stable after an intentional overdose?

options.A: Scolding the patient to prevent them from trying it again
options.B: Restricting all family members from visiting the bedside
options.C: Discharging the patient immediately without further delay
options.D: Arranging a psychiatric evaluation and providing a safe space

explanation: Holistic nursing means caring for the mind too! Intentional overdoses call for compassionate mental health support and a safe, non-judgmental environment. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T9#GNS125_U2_T9_h7)

question: What is a major downside of relying only on authority figures for your clinical decisions?

options.A: Institutional leaders have no clinical background
options.B: Authority figures are impossible to locate in a hospital
options.C: Senior nurses refuse to speak with junior staff
options.D: Experts may base views on custom rather than evidence

explanation: Even experienced experts can fall back on outdated habits if their views aren't backed by solid, current research. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T2#GNS217_U1_T2_h3)

question: What do we call a cancer that starts in the epithelial tissue lining body surfaces?

options.A: Sarcoma
options.B: Myeloma
options.C: Leukemia
options.D: Carcinoma

explanation: You're doing great! Carcinomas are the most common type of cancer because they start in the skin and the cells lining our internal organs and body surfaces. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a common mistake when setting objectives?

options.A: Creating vague statements without metrics
options.B: Consulting frontline staff during the drafting phase
options.C: Setting too many objectives at once
options.D: Setting targets in isolation from the team

explanation: Talking to your staff is a fantastic practice, not a mistake! The other choices are classic pitfalls to avoid. [learn more](GST321_U2_T1#GST321_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which part of the brain kicks off the reproductive hormone cycle by releasing GnRH?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Testis
options.C: Pituitary gland
options.D: Prostate gland

explanation: The hypothalamus is the master control center in the brain. It secretes GnRH to wake up the pituitary gland and start the hormone chain reaction. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T2#GNS121_U4_T2_h8)

question: Which of these is a major characteristic of adult learners during a teaching session?

options.A: They refuse to participate in group discussions or role play
options.B: They remember long lists of medical terms better than children
options.C: They need strict discipline and constant supervision from lecturers
options.D: They prefer to be actively involved in planning their learning goals

explanation: Brilliant! Adults love having a say in what and how they learn. They value their independence rather than just sitting quietly as passive listeners. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T10#GNS124_U5_T10_h2)

question: What minimum percentage of adherence is needed for antiretroviral therapy to work successfully?
explanation: You nailed it! Patients need to take at least 95% of their doses on time to keep the virus suppressed and stop resistance. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T13#GNS215_U6_T13_h4)

question: How can you find the median value using a finished ogive graph?

options.A: Calculate the difference between the first point and the last point
options.B: Count the total number of straight line segments in the polygon
options.C: Find the highest peak on the graph and read the number directly underneath
options.D: Locate 50 percent on the y-axis, move across to the line, and drop down to the x-axis

explanation: Brilliant! Since the median is the 50th percentile, finding 50% on the side and moving to the line guides you straight to the middle value below. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T11#GNS217_U4_T11_h5)

question: When is the best time to discuss family planning options with a patient receiving post-abortion care?

options.A: Before the patient is discharged from the clinical setting
options.B: Only after the patient experiences a second unplanned pregnancy
options.C: Refer them to a distant pharmacy without discussing options
options.D: Wait until six months have passed to avoid overwhelming them

explanation: Spot on! Bringing up family planning before discharge ensures the patient is protected against a quick repeat pregnancy while they are still connected to care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h5)

question: What is the main focus of the 'Study' phase?

options.A: Buying new computers for the nursing station
options.B: Firing staff members whose tests did not show improvement
options.C: Analyzing data and comparing results to initial predictions
options.D: Starting a brand new project without checking the old one

explanation: Fantastic! In the Study phase, we look at our notes to see if our new idea actually matched what we hoped would happen. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h5)

question: Which part of the brain is responsible for releasing Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH)?

options.A: The hypothalamus
options.B: The cerebral cortex
options.C: The cerebellum
options.D: The medulla oblongata

explanation: You got it! The hypothalamus acts as the master control center in the brain, pulsing out GnRH to kickstart reproductive development. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T13#GNS121_U5_T13_h2)

question: Why is reaching a consensus often preferred when working with village health committees on new health programs?

options.A: It ensures local stakeholders genuinely support and accept the program
options.B: It is the fastest possible way to make administrative decisions
options.C: It prevents any member from ever raising a question or concern
options.D: It allows the nurse leader to bypass community opinions entirely

explanation: Consensus means everyone agrees to support the decision, which builds strong community ownership and cooperation. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h4)

question: Why does a recipient's immune system try to attack a newly transplanted organ?

options.A: It panics over the physical pressure of the new blood flow
options.B: It causes a sudden crash in red blood cells
options.C: It spots foreign human leukocyte antigens (HLAs) on the donor cells
options.D: It reacts badly to the surgical stitches

explanation: Our immune systems are super protective! When they see foreign HLA markers on a donor organ that don't match the body's own, they sound the alarm and try to reject it. [learn more](GST114_U4_T7#GST114_U4_T7_h5)

question: What is the best way to care for a newborn baby's umbilical cord stump?

options.A: Applying strong iodine and native oils daily
options.B: Keeping it clean and dry without applying harsh substances
options.C: Covering it tightly with a waterproof plastic bandage
options.D: Washing it with medicated soap every single hour

explanation: Keep shining! Dry cord care is the gold standard—just keep it clean and dry and let it fall off naturally without putting oils or chemicals on it. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T021#GNS226_U3_T021_h5)

question: Which of these details is NOT necessary to write down in your notes after a blood transfusion?

options.A: The name of the blood donor's family members
options.B: The product serial number and volume given
options.C: The start and stop times of the infusion
options.D: The patient's post-transfusion vital signs

explanation: Donor privacy is key! Blood banks keep donor details strictly confidential, so they never appear in your patient's chart. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T18#GNS122_U1_T18_h8)

question: Which sign indicates that fresh fish is safe and good to buy?

options.A: Clear, bulging eyes and red gills
options.B: A strong, unpleasant ammonia smell
options.C: Sunken eyes and grey gills
options.D: A dull, sticky skin surface

explanation: Fresh fish typically has clear eyes, bright red gills, and a clean ocean scent rather than a foul odor. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h3)

question: What happens when you do a task for a patient who can easily do it themselves?

options.A: It steals their dignity and strength
options.B: It prevents accidental falls
options.C: It stops them from getting tired
options.D: It speeds up muscle recovery

explanation: Spot on! Always encourage patients to do what they can. Doing everything for them makes their muscles lazy and chips away at their independence. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h2)

question: What is the main job of the 'statement of the problem' in your proposal?

options.A: To list the names of every nurse working on the ward
options.B: To summarize the final conclusions of the study
options.C: To highlight the exact gap or issue requiring research
options.D: To advertise new medical equipment to the hospital

explanation: The problem statement tells your reader: 'Here is what we don't know yet, and here is why our study needs to fix it!' [learn more](GNS224_U3_T2#GNS224_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is an ethical dilemma involving money in nursing?

options.A: Deciding which nurse gets to attend a fully funded overseas conference
options.B: Balancing hospital cost-cutting with the duty to advocate for patients
options.C: Reporting a colleague who forgot to wash their hands before a procedure
options.D: Choosing whether to buy electronic tablets or paper charts for the ward

explanation: This is a classic challenge: nurses always want the best for their patients, but must navigate strict financial limits set by management. [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of giving antiretroviral therapy to an HIV-positive pregnant woman?

options.A: To speed up fetal bone growth in the third trimester
options.B: To prevent the mother from gaining excessive weight
options.C: To eliminate morning sickness symptoms completely
options.D: To prevent passing the virus from mother to child

explanation: Brilliant! Keeping the mother's viral load down drastically cuts down the chance of passing the virus to the baby (vertical transmission). [learn more](GNS215_U6_T13#GNS215_U6_T13_h7)

question: Why do red blood cells change into a sickle shape in this condition?

options.A: The bone marrow produces cells with too much iron and water inside them
options.B: Haemoglobin S molecules stick together to form rigid rods when they release oxygen
options.C: White blood cells attack and deform the healthy red blood cells
options.D: Excess sugar in the bloodstream causes the red blood cells to shrink and warp

explanation: When haemoglobin S delivers oxygen to body tissues, it clumps into stiff strands that distort the normal round cell into a crescent shape. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h1)

question: What do we call an infectious disease that jumps naturally from animals to humans?

options.A: Nosocomial infection
options.B: Idiopathic disease
options.C: Opportunistic pathogen
options.D: Zoonosis

explanation: A zoonotic disease (or zoonosis) is an infection that normally lives in animals but can cross over to infect humans. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why are Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs) sometimes prescribed for severe hypochondriasis?

options.A: To lower the overall intensity of obsessive health worries and treat depression
options.B: To cure any undiagnosed viral infections hiding in the bloodstream
options.C: To cause mild sedation so the patient sleeps through doctor appointments
options.D: To physically block pain receptors in the muscles and internal organs

explanation: SSRIs help balance the brain chemicals tied to anxiety and obsession, making it much easier for the patient to participate in therapy. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h7)

question: How long can a released egg survive and remain ready for fertilization?

options.A: 12 to 24 hours
options.B: 1 week
options.C: Up to 1 month
options.D: 3 to 5 days

explanation: The egg has a very short window of about 12 to 24 hours after ovulation to meet a sperm cell. Timing is everything! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T7#GNS121_U5_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary cause of varicose veins?

options.A: Atherosclerotic plaque blocking deep arteries
options.B: Too many red blood cells being made in the bone marrow
options.C: Sudden arterial spasm from cold weather
options.D: Damaged or weak valves inside the veins

explanation: When vein valves get tired or damaged, they can't close properly. Blood pools in the lower legs, stretching the veins out into those bumpy, twisted varicose lines. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T10#GNS213_U1_T10_h4)

question: What is the main goal of pasteurizing commercial milk?

options.A: To increase the natural sugar and fat percentages
options.B: To destroy all disease-causing pathogens safely
options.C: To remove every single living microbe and spore
options.D: To convert all liquid milk completely into cheese

explanation: You got it! Pasteurization uses heat to knock out harmful germs so the milk is safe to drink, even though it doesn't kill every single spore. [learn more](GST114_U3_T4#GST114_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why might a palliative patient feel severely short of breath even when their oxygen saturation is normal?

options.A: Pulse oximeters always give false readings in terminally ill patients
options.B: The patient is only pretending to panic to gain attention
options.C: Dyspnea is a subjective feeling influenced by many physical and emotional factors
options.D: Normal oxygen levels mean the lungs are working at full capacity

explanation: Breathlessness is a personal sensation that does not always match objective lab or monitor readings. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h4)

question: Why does staff resistance to change pose a major challenge to implementing a new ward plan?

options.A: Because it automatically increases the hospital annual financial budget
options.B: Because it forces managers to delete all previous institutional policies
options.C: Because nurses may refuse to adopt the new procedures, causing the plan to fail
options.D: Because it immediately stops all emergency patient admissions

explanation: If staff push back and refuse to cooperate with new routines, even the best-designed plan will fail in practice. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h6)

question: How does early marriage typically impact a young girl's social life?

options.A: It encourages her to travel freely for professional development
options.B: It grants her high social status and leadership roles among adults
options.C: It expands her network of supportive teenage friends
options.D: It isolates her from peers and ends her formal education

explanation: Early marriage usually takes girls out of school and confines them to home duties, cutting them off from friends and normal support systems. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T6#GNS225_U6_T6_h5)

question: Why must disaster planning focus heavily on local government areas?

options.A: National laws forbid federal agencies from entering disaster zones
options.B: Local councils have more advanced medical equipment than federal hospitals
options.C: Disasters happen locally and require immediate community-level action
options.D: Local governments are the only bodies allowed to receive foreign aid

explanation: You got it! Because emergencies hit specific communities directly, local prep ensures rescue and relief kick off instantly without waiting for outside help. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T8#GNS315_U1_T8_h1)

question: A new mother soaks two heavy pads in twenty minutes and feels dizzy. What should you suspect?

options.A: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.B: Normal postpartum lochia rubra
options.C: Delayed uterine subinvolution
options.D: Gestational trophoblastic disease

explanation: Rapid, heavy bleeding combined with dizziness is a classic sign of postpartum hemorrhage. Quick action is key here! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h3)

question: Which route of exposure is responsible for the highest number of accidental poisonings in young children?

options.A: Absorption
options.B: Inhalation
options.C: Ingestion
options.D: Injection

explanation: Young children naturally explore their environment by placing objects and liquids into their mouths, making swallowing the leading exposure route. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h2)

question: What is the main reason midwives and nurses measure fundal height during antenatal checks?

options.A: To estimate gestational age and monitor fetal growth
options.B: To calculate the total amount of amniotic fluid
options.C: To determine the exact birth weight of the baby
options.D: To check the strength of the uterine muscle walls

explanation: Correct! Fundal height in centimeters usually matches the weeks of pregnancy, helping us track if the baby is growing just right. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h3)

question: What is usually the very first sign of puerperal sepsis in a new mother?

options.A: Hair loss
options.B: Constipation
options.C: Weight gain
options.D: Fever

explanation: Always watch out for temperature spikes! A sudden fever is typically the earliest and most important warning sign that an infection is brewing postpartum. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T024#GNS226_U3_T024_h4)

question: Which global body defines nursing as autonomous and collaborative care for people of all ages in all settings?

options.A: West African Health Organization
options.B: International Council of Nurses
options.C: Red Cross International
options.D: World Medical Association

explanation: Spot on! The International Council of Nurses sets the global standard definition that highlights both our independent and teamwork roles in healthcare. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why is the hormone hCG so important right after a fertilized egg implants?

options.A: It triggers the immediate onset of active labor contractions
options.B: It stimulates the rapid production of red blood cells
options.C: It keeps progesterone levels up so the uterine lining stays strong
options.D: It directly causes morning sickness in the expectant mother

explanation: hCG acts like a cheerleader for the corpus luteum, telling it to keep pumping out progesterone so the womb stays cozy and ready for the baby. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T001#GNS226_U2_T001_h3)

question: A nurse researcher assigns hospital wards to receive a new handwashing training program by drawing lots. What experimental element is this?

options.A: Randomization
options.B: Manipulation
options.C: Data saturation
options.D: Blinding

explanation: Drawing lots means choice is left entirely to chance—that is classic randomization in action! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T4#GNS224_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the main job of normal lymphocytes in our body?

options.A: Fighting off infections and foreign invaders
options.B: Producing red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.C: Clotting blood to prevent bleeding
options.D: Carrying oxygen to body tissues

explanation: Think of lymphocytes as part of your body's security team! They are white blood cells that protect you against bacteria, viruses, and other germs. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T9#GNS311_U2_T9_h1)

question: Why is simple washing not considered true sterilization?

options.A: Soap chemically alters surgical steel and ruins the instruments
options.B: Washing only removes dirt and some microbes without killing spores
options.C: Cleaning actually introduces more bacteria to the equipment
options.D: Washing uses cold water which activates bacterial growth

explanation: Washing is a great first step to get the dirt off, but it leaves tough little spores behind. Sterilization finishes the job! [learn more](GST114_U2_T11#GST114_U2_T11_h1)

question: A surgical assistant holds tissue away so the surgeon can see clearly. What is this called?

options.A: Retracting
options.B: Suctioning
options.C: Catheterizing
options.D: Intubating

explanation: When assistants hold back organs or tissues to give a clear view, it's called 'retracting.' Picture holding curtains open wide so you can see inside! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h2)

question: What does a high Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP) level mostly point toward?

options.A: Severe acute viral hepatitis infection
options.B: Chronic kidney filtration failure
options.C: Bile duct obstruction or bone activity
options.D: Massive breakdown of red blood cells

explanation: Brilliant! ALP hangs out in the bile ducts and bones, so high numbers usually point your clinical suspicion toward biliary issues or bone growth/turnover. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T11#GNS221_U2_T11_h4)

question: Which of these is a major community stressor that can negatively impact mental health?

options.A: High neighborhood crime rates and financial instability
options.B: Living in a quiet suburban neighborhood with trees
options.C: Access to free community health clinics
options.D: Having too many public libraries in the local district

explanation: Constant financial worry and unsafe surroundings put a heavy, exhausting toll on a person's mental well-being. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T1#GNS314_U4_T1_h5)

question: What does an 'informed culture' depend on most in daily hospital work?

options.A: Strict rules that penalize any minor deviation
options.B: Leaving safety decisions entirely to hospital directors
options.C: Ignoring small mistakes that do not harm patients
options.D: An understanding of factors affecting safe patient care

explanation: Think of it as staying aware! An informed culture keeps all staff mindful of the everyday things—like fatigue or busy shifts—that can impact how safely we care for patients. [learn more](GST319_U6_T6#GST319_U6_T6_h2)

question: Which of these is a common informal support system in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: Private pharmaceutical companies
options.B: Extended family compounds and religious bodies
options.C: Teaching hospital psychiatric wards
options.D: Government health insurance offices

explanation: In Nigeria, our strongest safety nets are often informal—our extended family ties, local churches, mosques, and community groups. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h8)

question: A junior nurse is told to do a dressing change a certain way simply because 'that is how we've always done it here.' What type of inquiry is this?

options.A: Traditional and authority-based inquiry
options.B: Randomized controlled testing
options.C: Empirical scientific inquiry
options.D: Systematic qualitative inquiry

explanation: Relying on past custom and instructions from senior staff without checking the literature is traditional and authority-based inquiry. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T2#GNS217_U1_T2_h3)

question: A community health nurse wants to help reduce FGM rates in a rural village. Which strategy works best for lasting change?

options.A: Ignoring the practice to avoid offending cultural traditions
options.B: Performing mild pricks in the clinic to keep traditions alive safely
options.C: Engaging local leaders and educators in discussions about health risks
options.D: Arresting every mother without talking to the community

explanation: Brilliant! Real, lasting change happens when you work hand-in-hand with the community to shift mindsets and choose health together. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T4#GNS225_U6_T4_h8)

question: How should you position your patient right after a thoracentesis is finished?

options.A: On the unaffected side
options.B: Prone on the abdomen
options.C: Flat on the back
options.D: Flat on the affected side

explanation: You nailed it! Having them lie on the good (unaffected) side helps the tiny puncture site seal up and lets the treated lung expand fully. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h5)

question: Why is general supportive care often more critical than finding an antidote right away when someone is poisoned?

options.A: Supportive care keeps vital organs working while the body clears the toxin
options.B: Most poisons have strong antidotes available immediately
options.C: Antidotes only work if given within two minutes of exposure
options.D: Antidotes are too expensive to keep in most rural hospitals

explanation: Great thinking! Since we don't have a magical antidote for every single poison out there, keeping the patient's breathing and heart going buys enough time for their body to naturally process and clear the toxin. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T10#GNS125_U2_T10_h1)

question: Which nursing action directly attacks a biological germ inside a patient's body?

options.A: Screening building ventilation systems
options.B: Teaching mothers how to wash their hands
options.C: Administering a prescribed course of antibiotics
options.D: Ensuring proper disposal of community waste

explanation: Medicines like antibiotics go right inside the patient to fight off and destroy the invading bacteria. Simple and direct! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T78#GNS214_U1_T78_h7)

question: Which acid-base imbalance is most likely to happen during severe, long-lasting diarrhoea?

options.A: Respiratory alkalosis from breathing in too much oxygen
options.B: Metabolic acidosis from losing bicarbonate in the stool
options.C: Respiratory acidosis from slowing down breathing rates
options.D: Metabolic alkalosis from retaining too much stomach acid

explanation: Our lower gut secretions are packed with bicarbonate (our body's natural buffer). Losing loads of these fluids means we lose our buffer, leading to metabolic acidosis. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why shouldn't you fill a sharps container past its fill line?

options.A: It prevents the hospital from recycling the plastic material
options.B: It makes the container too heavy for the waste collectors
options.C: It increases the risk of accidental needle-stick injuries
options.D: It causes the plastic walls of the container to melt

explanation: You got it! Overfilling sharps bins means needles start poking out or pushing against the lid, putting anyone handling the bin at high risk of a needle-stick injury. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h4)

question: Before giving another dose of magnesium sulfate, which clinical sign must you check first?

options.A: Level of blood glucose
options.B: Size of the liver and spleen
options.C: Presence of knee-jerk patellar reflexes
options.D: Fetal heart rate variability

explanation: Awesome job! Losing the knee-jerk reflex is an early warning sign that magnesium is building up too much in the body, well before breathing slows down. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h5)

question: A patient nods and says yes to everything you say while looking very confused. What should you do next?

options.A: Ask the patient to explain the instructions back in their own words
options.B: Write the instructions down and leave the room immediately
options.C: Speak much louder in case they have a hearing problem
options.D: Assume they understand because they agreed verbally

explanation: Using the teach-back method checks real understanding instead of relying on polite nods. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h2)

question: Why should nurses team up with traditional and religious leaders in community campaigns against GBV?

options.A: Because traditional leaders provide direct funding for hospital equipment
options.B: Because these leaders hold significant influence in shaping community norms and attitudes
options.C: Because religious leaders take over medical duties during emergencies
options.D: Because nurses are not legally permitted to speak publicly outside hospitals

explanation: Well done! Community leaders are respected voices; partnering with them helps change cultural attitudes and gets people on board with prevention. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T8#GNS312_U4_T8_h9)

question: A clinic nurse notices a sudden spike in measles cases in the monthly records. What is the best practical step to take?

options.A: Blame community members for refusing to bring their children to the clinic
options.B: Hide the registers in a locked drawer so nobody notices the increase
options.C: Alert district health authorities and organize an emergency vaccination outreach
options.D: Stop recording patient visits until the rainy season is completely over

explanation: That's how data saves lives! Spotting a trend in your records lets you take quick public health action. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T21#GNS225_U2_T21_h6)

question: Why must you scrub an IV port with an alcohol swab before hooking up a syringe?

options.A: It prevents the plastic port from cracking under high pump pressure
options.B: It chemically activates the medication inside the attached syringe
options.C: It removes bacteria and prevents microorganisms from entering the bloodstream
options.D: It lubricates the rubber seal so the syringe connects more smoothly

explanation: Brilliant! Friction from scrubbing wipes away germs so they don't hitch a ride straight into the patient's bloodstream. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T3#GNS212_U4_T3_h7)

question: In mass casualty triage, what does a RED tag mean?

options.A: Minor cuts and bruises that can be treated with basic self-care methods
options.B: Immediate, life-threatening injuries requiring urgent intervention to save life
options.C: Stable injuries that can safely wait several hours for medical attention
options.D: Catastrophic injuries where the patient has little chance of survival

explanation: Red means 'Right now!' These patients have severe, life-threatening injuries and need our immediate care to survive. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T7#GNS315_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why are graphs and visual charts so helpful for busy nurses?

options.A: They make complex trends and changes easy to understand quickly
options.B: They prevent patients from seeing their own vital sign records
options.C: They replace all written patient progress notes in the medical record
options.D: They are legally required by hospital management for promotion

explanation: Pictures save time! A quick glance at a graph lets a busy nurse see trends instantly without having to crunch a bunch of numbers. [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h4)

question: How do strong social support systems help protect a person's mental health?

options.A: They eliminate all stressful events from happening in life
options.B: They ensure the person never experiences sadness
options.C: They replace the need for professional psychiatric medication
options.D: They provide emotional validation and practical help during crises

explanation: Having friends or family who listen and stand by you makes heavy burdens feel much lighter. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T1#GNS314_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the main difference between proactive and reactive risk strategies?

options.A: Proactive strategies cost more money than any reactive hospital investigation
options.B: Proactive strategies are handled by doctors, while reactive strategies are handled by nurses
options.C: Proactive strategies act before harm happens, while reactive strategies respond after harm occurs
options.D: Proactive strategies focus on equipment, while reactive strategies focus on staff

explanation: The timing is the key difference: stopping an accident beforehand versus cleaning up the pieces after an accident takes place. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary trigger for hypovolemic shock?

options.A: An infection spreading through the bloodstream
options.B: A rapid drop in circulating blood volume
options.C: An acute blockage in the coronary arteries
options.D: A sudden spike in blood pressure

explanation: Hypovolemic shock happens when the body loses a massive amount of fluid or blood, leaving the circulatory system with too little volume to fill the blood vessels. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h2)

question: Why does taking multiple medications increase a patient's risk of falling?

options.A: It frequently causes dizziness, sedation, or confusion
options.B: It permanently damages the inner ear balance organs
options.C: It directly weakens the bones in the feet
options.D: It increases the body's overall physical weight

explanation: Side effects from combining several drugs can alter mental alertness and physical stability, leading to unsteady walking. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h1)

question: A healthy newborn cries hard and briefly gets a little blue around the lips. Why might this happen with the foramen ovale?

options.A: Vigorous crying can raise right-sided heart pressure and reopen the valve temporarily
options.B: The umbilical cord was clamped too tightly, cutting off systemic oxygen
options.C: Crying stops blood flow through the lungs completely for several minutes
options.D: The ductus arteriosus has permanently scarred too early in development

explanation: Don't worry, this is normal! Straining from a big cry can temporarily spike pressure on the right side of the heart, gently pushing that recently closed flap open for just a second. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T007#GNS226_U2_T007_h3)

question: How does a nurse properly assess a patient's resting muscle tone?

options.A: By asking the patient to push hard against the nurse's hand
options.B: By observing the patient walk across the hospital room
options.C: By measuring the circumference of the limb with a tape
options.D: By feeling the resistance of the muscle during a passive stretch

explanation: Muscle tone is the resting tension of a muscle. You check this by gently moving the patient's limb for them and feeling how the muscle resists. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h3)

question: What does the vital infection control rule 'one needle, one syringe, one time' mean for your daily practice?

options.A: Injection equipment must be used for only one patient and never reused
options.B: Syringes can be reused if they are washed with soap and water
options.C: Multiple patients can share a medication vial if a new needle is attached
options.D: Nurses should change needles between patients but keep the same syringe

explanation: It's simple and non-negotiable: a fresh, sterile needle and syringe for every single patient, every single time. You've got this rule down! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h6)

question: A nurse notices that a postoperative surgical wound is increasingly red, warm, and draining foul-smelling pus. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

options.A: Wait until the patient's scheduled discharge day to mention it
options.B: Assume this is a normal healing process and take no action
options.C: Report the findings and document them clearly for the care team
options.D: Apply a dry bandage and advise the patient not to look at it

explanation: Prompt reporting and documentation ensure the medical team can investigate and treat a potential surgical site infection early. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h9)

question: Which of these is NOT a common cause of neurasthenia?

options.A: Overwhelming family responsibilities
options.B: Eating a high-protein diet
options.C: Severe occupational strain
options.D: Chronic financial hardship

explanation: Nice one! Eating healthy food doesn't cause nervous exhaustion. Money worries, work stress, and family pressures are the real triggers here. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T9#GNS314_U2_T9_h3)

question: What critical warning sign must you teach a patient who is taking hormonal reproductive medications?

options.A: Temporary fatigue in the evening
options.B: Sudden chest pain or leg swelling
options.C: Mild changes in hair texture
options.D: Slight increase in daily appetite

explanation: You nailed it! Hormones can raise the risk of blood clots, so chest pain or a swollen leg are major red flags patients must report immediately. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T14#GNS311_U1_T14_h6)

question: What does a family's ability to buy food mainly depend on?

options.A: Local government policies on soil fertilization.
options.B: Total income, employment stability, and market food prices.
options.C: Global weather patterns and international shipping laws.
options.D: The distance from the nearest agricultural research center.

explanation: Exactly! Purchasing power simply means how much money is coming into the house compared to how much food actually costs in the market. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T031#GNS227_U2_T031_h2)

question: Which detail is most important to include in your notes when charting routine hair care?

options.A: The exact minute the hair drying process started
options.B: Condition of the scalp and any abnormal findings
options.C: The total cost of the hair care products used
options.D: The exact brand of shampoo preferred by the nurse

explanation: Always focus your documentation on clear clinical facts, such as how the scalp looks and any unusual signs you spot. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h6)

question: How do certain bacteria and fungi manage to survive harsh sun and dry air up in the atmosphere?

options.A: They grow wings to fly away from sunny areas
options.B: They absorb all the pollution particles to feed themselves
options.C: They immediately transform into non-living chemical gases
options.D: They produce protective structures like spores or thick outer coats

explanation: Correct! Spores and tough coats act like a shield, keeping microbes safe until they land somewhere nice. [learn more](GST114_U6_T7#GST114_U6_T7_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe way to manage community medical waste?

options.A: Ensuring sharps containers are sealed before final disposal
options.B: Using puncture-resistant safety boxes for all used needles
options.C: Incinerating medical waste under controlled high temperatures
options.D: Throwing used syringes into ordinary household plastic garbage bags

explanation: Household bags easily puncture, exposing trash collectors and the public to contaminated needles. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why is it so important to use simple, everyday language when teaching mothers at the clinic?

options.A: It prevents mothers from asking questions about immunization schedules
options.B: It ensures clear understanding and correct execution of home care practices
options.C: It saves clinic time so the nurse can finish work much earlier
options.D: It guarantees that mothers will memorize the entire clinic manual

explanation: You nailed it! Clear, jargon-free talk ensures mothers truly understand and can care for their babies safely at home. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T2#GNS225_U3_T2_h7)

question: Which of these specimens should NOT be put in the refrigerator if transport is delayed?

options.A: Routine urine collection
options.B: Swab of a skin wound
options.C: Stool sample for parasites
options.D: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)

explanation: CSF contains very delicate germs that the cold can easily kill. These urgent samples need to stay at room temperature! [learn more](GST114_U5_T1#GST114_U5_T1_h7)

question: In a patient health history, what do we mean by the 'chief complaint'?

options.A: The primary reason the patient is seeking care, in their own words
options.B: The surgical history from the patient's childhood
options.C: The final medical diagnosis written by the attending physician
options.D: A complete list of every prescription medication the patient takes

explanation: Spot-on! The chief complaint is simply the main trouble or symptom that brought the patient to the clinic, written using what they tell you. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T2#GNS222_U1_T2_h3)

question: What happens inside the body of a patient with severe burns that makes a high-protein diet critical for their survival?

options.A: Hypermetabolism causes rapid tissue breakdown and protein loss
options.B: Bones instantly release all stored calcium into the blood
options.C: The kidneys stop filtering waste products completely
options.D: The digestive tract absorbs fewer vitamins than normal

explanation: Severe burns put the body into an extreme 'overdrive' state where muscle and tissue break down rapidly. High protein helps fight off this severe wasting. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h3)

question: According to Herzberg, which of these is a true 'motivator' rather than just a hygiene factor?

options.A: Getting regular praise and recognition for good clinical work
options.B: Receiving a stable, predictable monthly salary
options.C: Working in a clean, air-conditioned nursing station
options.D: Following clear hospital policies and safety rules

explanation: You nailed it! Recognition makes us feel good about our actual work and drives us to do better, while salary and nice rooms just keep us from complaining. [learn more](GST321_U3_T5#GST321_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which group of vitamins is known as fat-soluble?

options.A: Vitamins A, D, E, and K
options.B: Vitamin C and the B-complex group
options.C: Calcium, iron, and potassium
options.D: Amino acids and plant extracts

explanation: Think of vitamins A, D, E, and K as the ones that dissolve in fat and can hang out in our body's fatty tissues and liver for later use. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h2)

question: When you hear 'quantitative research', what kind of data immediately comes to mind?

options.A: Unstructured audio recordings of interviews
options.B: Numerical data and measurable variables
options.C: Handwritten patient diary entries
options.D: Detailed personal stories and life histories

explanation: Think 'Q for Quantity'! Quantitative research is all about numbers, measurements, and stats to find answers. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T3#GNS224_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which professional helps a client adapt their living space by introducing tools like customized eating utensils?

options.A: Surgeon
options.B: Pharmacologist
options.C: Radiologic technologist
options.D: Occupational therapist

explanation: Occupational therapists specialize in helping clients adapt their daily activities and living spaces to maintain their independence. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h5)

question: Which of these is a critical warning sign that a pregnant woman must report straight away?

options.A: Occasional mild heartburn
options.B: Decreased fetal movement
options.C: Increased fatigue in the evening
options.D: Mild swelling in the ankles

explanation: Always teach mums to track their baby's kicks! Fewer movements can mean the baby is stressed and needs an immediate check-up. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h6)

question: What does a 4+ reflex score with jerky muscle spasms (clonus) usually point to?

options.A: Normal healthy muscle recovery
options.B: Complete peripheral nerve damage
options.C: Central nervous system pathology
options.D: Severe dehydration and low sodium

explanation: Extremely brisk reflexes with clonus mean there is likely an issue or irritation in the central nervous system (brain or spinal cord). [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h7)

question: What is the final practical step you should take before using a brand new checklist in a major study?

options.A: Translate the checklist into three new languages
options.B: Publish the checklist in a nursing journal
options.C: Pilot test the draft in a small trial run
options.D: File the checklist away in a locked cabinet

explanation: Always test-run your tool first! A pilot test helps catch confusing questions or missing steps before you start the real study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T23#GNS224_U1_T23_h4)

question: What is the main goal of pharmacovigilance in healthcare?

options.A: Marketing new pharmaceutical products to regional hospitals
options.B: Detecting, assessing, and preventing adverse drug effects
options.C: Speeding up the clinical drug trial approval process
options.D: Calculating the financial cost of manufactured medications

explanation: Pharmacovigilance is the ongoing safety monitoring process designed to catch and prevent drug-related harm. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h8)

question: What does the concept of 'total pain' in palliative care include?

options.A: Severe physical pain that is completely resistant to opioid drugs
options.B: Pain that only affects the neurological and musculoskeletal systems
options.C: Physical discomfort combined with emotional, social, and spiritual distress
options.D: Temporary discomfort caused strictly by diagnostic medical tests

explanation: Total pain acknowledges that physical suffering is deeply influenced by a person's mental state, social worries, and spiritual fears. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h2)

question: Which amino acid is the starting point for making catecholamines and thyroid hormones?

options.A: Alanine
options.B: Tyrosine
options.C: Glycine
options.D: Tryptophan

explanation: Tyrosine is the key building block amino acid used to manufacture important hormones like adrenaline and your thyroid hormones. One step at a time, you're learning it! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T10#GNS211_U1_T10_h3)

question: Why does salivary amylase stop working once food reaches the stomach?

options.A: The stomach absorbs all the leftover saliva immediately
options.B: The food spends too little time in the stomach
options.C: The strong acid in the stomach deactivates the enzyme
options.D: Other enzymes replace it and make it unnecessary

explanation: Salivary amylase loves the neutral mouth environment, but the harsh acid in the stomach shuts it right down. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h2)

question: Why do experts recommend combining medication with behavioral counseling instead of using medication alone?

options.A: Counseling addresses the psychological habits while medication treats physical cravings
options.B: Government health insurance policies forbid giving out prescriptions alone
options.C: Medications are too expensive for patients to buy without counseling
options.D: Medications only work if the patient attends weekly support group meetings

explanation: Tackling both the physical craving and the mental habit gives the patient the absolute best chance at success. You're thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h7)

question: Which of these conditions is NOT typically confused with a benign cervical ectropion during an exam?

options.A: Uterine fibroids located in the myometrium
options.B: Benign cervical polyps protruding from the os
options.C: Early malignant tumors of the cervix
options.D: Cervicitis caused by sexually transmitted organisms

explanation: Fibroids sit deep inside the muscular wall of the uterus, way past the surface of the cervix, so they won't look like a red patch on the outer cervix. You nailed it! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h7)

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluating a health communication program?

options.A: Monitoring costs money, while evaluation is always completely free
options.B: Monitoring is done by patients, while evaluation is done by politicians
options.C: Monitoring tracks daily activities, while evaluation measures long-term impact
options.D: Monitoring focuses on drugs, while evaluation focuses only on surgery

explanation: Well done! Monitoring looks at what is happening day-to-day, while evaluation checks the overall success at the end. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary function of a hospital journal club?

options.A: To help nurses read, discuss, and understand research articles together
options.B: To discipline nurses who make mistakes during procedures
options.C: To write brand new research papers for international publishing
options.D: To raise money for buying new ward equipment

explanation: Brilliant! Journal clubs are cozy, supportive spaces where we break down studies together so everyone can learn without feeling intimidated. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h5)

question: When stripping a dirty bed, what is the correct way to handle the used linen?

options.A: Roll it inward toward the center to trap dirt and microbes
options.B: Shake each sheet vigorously to remove loose hair
options.C: Toss the bundle across the room into the laundry chute
options.D: Fold each sheet into a square and place on the floor

explanation: You nailed it! Rolling the dirty linen inward traps skin flakes, dust, and germs so they don't fly into the air or onto your clothes. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h4)

question: A child's weight-for-length falls way below the minus two Z-score on the growth chart. What does this mean?

options.A: Advanced neurological maturity
options.B: Chronic skeletal stunting
options.C: Acute malnutrition or wasting
options.D: Normal developmental variation

explanation: You're doing great! Weight-for-length compares mass to height. A very low score means the child has recently lost weight and is too thin for their height—a sign of wasting. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h5)

question: How does financial hardship usually change how people seek healthcare in Nigeria?

options.A: Patients rely entirely on free federal government prescriptions
options.B: Patients bypass local clinics to visit expensive foreign hospitals
options.C: Patients delay seeking care until their illnesses become advanced
options.D: Patients demand immediate surgical interventions for minor pains

explanation: That's correct. Financial constraints often force people to wait and hope symptoms go away on their own, which unfortunately means they often arrive at the clinic very sick. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the purpose of conducting routine preventive maintenance on hospital backup generators?

options.A: To ensure uninterrupted power for critical life-support equipment during outages
options.B: To replace all the lighting fixtures in the administrative offices annually
options.C: To lower the daily electricity bill charged by the public utility company
options.D: To increase the speed at which elevators transport patients between floors

explanation: When public power fails, backup generators must kick in instantly to keep life-saving machines like ventilators running smoothly. Regular checks make sure they never let us down! [learn more](GST321_U4_T5#GST321_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which of the following findings belongs in the review of systems?

options.A: A patient reporting occasional dizziness when standing up
options.B: A nurse measuring a blood pressure reading of 120/80 mmHg
options.C: A laboratory report showing a high white blood cell count
options.D: A surgeon finding an inflamed appendix during an operation

explanation: Dizziness reported by the patient is a subjective symptom, which is what the review of systems records. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h6)

question: During a building collapse with dozens of victims, a patient with severe, fatal injuries gets an expectant (black) tag. Why do we do this?

options.A: Because nurses are not legally allowed to touch trauma patients outdoors
options.B: To preserve scarce medical supplies for victims who have a better chance of survival
options.C: Because minor injuries always take legal precedence over head trauma
options.D: To punish the patient for not wearing safety equipment

explanation: This is one of the hardest parts of nursing, but when supplies are limited, we must focus our efforts where we can genuinely save lives. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h4)

question: What type of feedback loop is most often used to keep hormone levels balanced?

options.A: Positive feedback
options.B: Negative feedback
options.C: Cyclic feedback
options.D: Neutral feedback

explanation: You nailed it! Negative feedback acts like a thermostat, turning hormone production up or down to keep things stable. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T1#GNS211_U1_T1_h7)

question: A patient presents to the clinic complaining of bleeding after sexual intercourse and a foul-smelling vaginal discharge. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Advise her to start taking heavy doses of oral iron supplements immediately
options.B: Instruct her to apply medicated vaginal creams every night for a month
options.C: Reassure her that this is a normal part of aging and send her home
options.D: Perform a detailed health history and facilitate a pelvic examination by the doctor

explanation: Post-coital bleeding requires prompt clinical investigation and visualization of the cervix to rule out malignancy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h4)

question: A patient with an arm cast complains of an intense itch deep inside. What advice should you give?

options.A: Pour a small amount of baby oil down the cast opening to soothe the skin
options.B: Insert a clean knitting needle gently down the side to scratch the itchy spot
options.C: Use a cool hair dryer breeze directed into the cast opening to relieve itching
options.D: Submerge the entire arm in warm soapy water until the itching stops

explanation: A cool breeze from a hair dryer is a safe trick to ease itching. Never stick objects inside the cast—they can break skin or get stuck! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is the main reason for plotting a child's weight on a growth chart during clinic visits?

options.A: To check if the child needs immediate dental surgery
options.B: To calculate the exact adult height of the child
options.C: To determine how much money the family earns
options.D: To detect faltering growth early before severe malnutrition develops

explanation: Spot on! Growth charts let us catch weight drops or slow growth early so we can step in long before severe malnutrition sets in. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h4)

question: What is the main goal of using traction for a fracture?

options.A: To permanently replace damaged bone tissue with artificial metal rods
options.B: To apply a pulling force that aligns bone fragments and reduces muscle spasms
options.C: To dissolve blood clots that form inside the injured blood vessels
options.D: To completely seal open wounds and prevent bacterial skin infections

explanation: Traction uses gentle, steady weights and ropes to calm tight, spasming muscles and pull the broken bone pieces back into their proper line. Clever nursing care! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T4#GNS112_U7_T4_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of adolescent counseling corners in primary health centers?

options.A: Providing a safe space for youths to seek guidance on emotional struggles
options.B: Isolating sick children from the rest of the community
options.C: Providing mandatory legal representation for arrested teenagers
options.D: Holding young offenders in secure custody awaiting court trials

explanation: You got it! Counseling corners offer teenagers a confidential place to talk through stress and peer pressure before things get out of hand. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T4#GNS225_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is the main job of a primary health care facility?

options.A: To serve as the first point of contact for community health needs
options.B: To train resident doctors and medical specialists
options.C: To provide long-term care for chronic psychiatric disorders
options.D: To perform major surgical operations like brain surgery

explanation: Primary health centers are right there in the community. They are the friendly first stop for everyday health needs and prevention. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h2)

question: What are the classic warning signs of peritonitis in a patient getting IP therapy?

options.A: A high fever accompanied by a persistent dry cough
options.B: Sudden swelling and redness of the lower legs
options.C: Cloudy effluent drainage and severe abdominal pain
options.D: Complete inability to speak or swallow food

explanation: Spot on! If the drained fluid looks cloudy instead of clear, paired with bad belly pain, it's a huge red flag for peritonitis (infection). [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h6)

question: Why do health workers treat gender-based violence as a major public health emergency?

options.A: It only affects women living in rural environments
options.B: It primarily places financial strain on hospital pharmacies
options.C: It causes widespread physical and psychological harm across communities
options.D: It is classified as a rare infectious disease outbreak

explanation: You got it! Because it hurts so many people physically and emotionally, healthcare systems treat it as a top priority to keep communities safe. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T23#GNS225_U5_T23_h1)

question: What is a key focus when nursing an expectant mother who has chronic kidney disease?

options.A: Administering prophylactic dialysis starting in the first trimester
options.B: Strict blood pressure monitoring and medication adherence support
options.C: Restricting fluid intake entirely to prevent maternal edema
options.D: Encouraging a high-protein diet to replace lost urinary nutrients

explanation: Keeping blood pressure in check takes the pressure off the kidneys and keeps the placenta happy and well-supplied with blood. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T007#GNS226_U4_T007_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of secondary prevention in healthcare?

options.A: Long-term physical rehabilitation
options.B: Early detection and treatment
options.C: Providing end-of-life comfort care
options.D: Stopping disease before it starts

explanation: Secondary prevention catches health issues early through screening so treatment can stop the disease from getting worse. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h1)

question: What major nutrient do legumes like cowpeas (beans) and bambara groundnuts bring to our local pots?

options.A: Fat-soluble vitamins
options.B: Saturated animal fats
options.C: Plant-based protein
options.D: Simple sugars

explanation: Exactly right! Legumes and beans are fantastic, budget-friendly sources of protein, especially when meat isn't within reach. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T007#GNS227_U3_T007_h4)

question: Which group of helminths has a cylindrical, unsegmented body shape?

options.A: Trematodes
options.B: Cestodes
options.C: Nematodes
options.D: Protozoa

explanation: Think of nematodes as the classic roundworms—they have that smooth, cylindrical, unsegmented body shape you talk about in class! [learn more](GST114_U3_T6#GST114_U3_T6_h2)

question: What does the 'M' stand for in the SMART objective framework used in healthcare management?

options.A: Mandatory
options.B: Managed
options.C: Medical
options.D: Measurable

explanation: Objectives must include quantifiable metrics so staff can clearly tell if they are succeeding. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h4)

question: A head nurse times how long it takes staff to complete morning vitals to eliminate wasted steps. Which management approach is being used?

options.A: Contingency approach
options.B: Systems theory
options.C: Scientific management
options.D: Human relations theory

explanation: Using time studies and analyzing physical movements to optimize workflow is the core of scientific management. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the correct step to take the moment a sharps container hits its fill line?

options.A: Leave the lid open for the next shift to use
options.B: Press the contents down firmly with your hand
options.C: Lock the lid securely and prepare for disposal
options.D: Empty the contents into a regular black bin

explanation: Locking the lid right away stops accidental spills and keeps protruding needles from injuring anyone. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h6)

question: In livestock farming, what do we call a disease that can jump between animals and humans?

options.A: A plant infection caused by heavy rainfall
options.B: A mechanical failure of milking equipment
options.C: An illness that can spread between animals and humans
options.D: A vitamin deficiency found only in farm workers

explanation: Zoonotic diseases are infections that naturally pass from animals to us. Think of illnesses like bird flu or rabies! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T024#GNS227_U2_T024_h3)

question: A nurse throws an expired bottle of liquid antibiotic into the regular office dustbin. What type of sorting mistake happened here?

options.A: Infectious waste placed in pathological waste
options.B: Sharps waste placed in chemical waste containers
options.C: General waste placed in hazardous containment
options.D: Pharmaceutical waste placed in general waste

explanation: Medicines and drugs are pharmaceutical waste. They need special disposal methods and should never be mixed with everyday office trash. [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h2)
